text:
Iris: Quick note: kerberos-int8 onboarding results came back flaky on short queries. recall@1 fell from 0.64 -> 0.49 on our 8k shortseq holdout. Posting the run summary and a few checks.

Sam: Oof. Short queries are often the canary. Can you paste the exact eval command + config?

Iris: Ran: `python -m evals.run --model kerberos-int8 --holdout-size 8000 --query-length-max 16 --k 1,5,10 --index hnsw`
Config snippets: `quantization: per_tensor symmetric, output_norm: l2, whitening: true (apply)`

Rafi: If whitening was applied, confirm the mean/variance used were from float model outputs not the quantized scale. Sometimes we accidentally compute whitening on already-quantized vectors.

Iris: Good point. I pulled the saved tensors and double-checked: whitening used float checkpoints. But noticed scale factors (max abs per-tensor) vary a lot across embedding dims.

Sam: That smells like per-tensor symmetric is losing granularity. Try per-channel asymmetric or per-channel symmetric if available. Also try dequantizing back to float for similarity computations: `emb = dequantize(int8_emb, scale, zp)`.

Iris: Ran two quick replays: (A) per-channel symmetric + dequantize->float, (B) per-channel asymmetric + bias-correction.
Results: A recall@1 0.60, recall@5 0.81. B recall@1 0.61, recall@5 0.82. So per-channel helps but still ~3 pts down vs float.

Tanya: Did you inspect cosine vs L2? For short queries cosine is often more stable if magnitudes compress during quantization.

Iris: Yes. Cosine float recall@1 0.64 -> int8 per-channel cosine 0.62 (much better). L2 shows the bigger gap. I attached a tiny PNG with cosine angle histograms and a difference heatmap between float and int8 similarity matrices: http://artifacts/kerberos/shortseq/heatmap.png

eval-bot: job 90211 finished (kerberos-int8-shortseq). Alert: shortseq-recall@1 below regression threshold. CI: http://ci.internal/90211. See artifacts.

Rafi: Two more quick checks: (1) Increase ef_search on the HNSW index (we use ef_search=128 by default for eval). Short queries sometimes need ef_search=256 to surface nearest neighbors. (2) Try norm-preserving quant, i.e., quantize after L2-normalizing vectors if your pipeline allows.

Iris: Bumped ef_search -> 256 and re-ran per-channel asymmetric + dequant. recall@1 -> 0.63, recall@5 -> 0.83. So index params were amplifying the apparent quality drop.

Sam: Nice. For the onboarding doc we should: recommend per-channel quant + dequant->float for similarity metrics, add a shortseq check in the preflight, and document index sensitivity (ef_search). I'll sketch a PR.

Tanya: Also add a short notebook showing: 1) L2 distribution shift, 2) cosine angle CDF, 3) nearest-neighbor rank swap examples (show queries where top-1 changed). Helps reviewers understand whether it's metric vs semantic failure.

Iris: On it. I'll push a tiny notebook and link it in the run. For follow-ups: test norm-after-quant vs norm-before-quant and try 6-bit dynamic if we need tighter memory/payloads.

Rafi: Agreed. One more thing if you see large zero-point drifts across dims that's a red flag for per-tensor. Per-channel solved it here. Good to capture a short checklist in onboarding.

Iris: Checklist entry saved. Closing thread, will ping when PRs + notebook are up. :rocket:
